summary: Hook rule files live in read-only /usr/lib/flightctl/hooks.d/<hook>/ (baked into the image) or writable /etc/flightctl/hooks.d/<hook>/; names must be lower case, both locations merge, files run in lexical order, /etc overrides same-named /usr files, and actions run sequentially with later actions skipped after a failure.
questions: Where do I put Edge Manager lifecycle hook rule files?
Which hook directory takes precedence, /etc or /usr?
In what order are hook rule files processed?
What happens to later actions if one hook action fails?
